criterion.standard: counts it worthwhile only if something he's told gets carried on by someone who heard it from him
criterion.wasted_life: one spent singing the same old verses and never once adding a true line of his own
criterion.trusts: what's actually been written down about a story, not just how it's sung this week
criterion.distrusts: a verse that changes every time you hear it, with no one keeping the true version

routines.routine_actions: plays most nights for whoever's drinking, works new verses about the town's revival in between the old standards
performs for the crowds on market days, trades a song for whatever a listener can spare
makes the trip back to Terfila now and then to trade verses with the bards there and see what's changed

arc.premise: Nicolopaulo wants to compose the first proper telling of Tyrnea's revival - not tavern gossip stitched together, but a real piece people will still be singing after the builders and professors who lived it are gone. Resolution: he finishes it and hears it sung back to him by someone who wasn't there for the telling, or it fades after one season same as every other tavern song.
